home.title: Home
home.name: Demian Kong
home.headline: Growing agent platforms. Verified scientific tool use.
home.bio: I build systems that turn human needs into executable, reusable capabilities. My work spans scientific database agents and Chrona, a local-first platform where agents create and revise software modules that persist beyond a single conversation.
home.researchQuestion: How can agents turn changing human needs into lasting capabilities—and keep those capabilities useful as their platform evolves?
highlights: Creator and sole developer of Chrona: a growing software platform for humans and agents.
Founder and lead developer of Dingent: tool-using agents across eight CNCB biological data resources.
Co-first author of two Nucleic Acids Research papers; first-listed co-first author of the Dingent bioRxiv preprint.

about.title: About
about.intro: I am a bioinformatics M.S. graduate and systems builder working on LLM agents, growing software platforms, and scientific data access. My path from pharmacy and experimental biology to multi-omics analysis and agent engineering shapes the questions I pursue: how to connect domain meaning, executable actions, and evidence.

education.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) / CNCB
details: Thesis: Research and Development of an Agent Framework for Bioinformatics Data Retrieval Based on Large Language Models.
Research connected configurable agent workflows, biological database retrieval, and query verification.
Thesis research on the role and mechanism of MKP5 in hepatic fibrosis, combining experimental models with bioinformatic analysis.
Led a provincial undergraduate innovation project in chemical synthesis and crystallography.

interests: Capability growth: how can agents extend a software platform to meet changing human needs with persistent, reusable modules?
Verified tool use: how can executable checks keep agent claims within the scope of retrieved evidence and tool execution?
Evaluation over time: how can query verification, oracle-free consistency checks, and cross-version tests assess more than isolated task success?
Scientific AI: how can domain-aware retrieval and protein–language modelling connect biological data with useful computational tools?
toolkit: Agent systems: LangGraph, MCP, checkpointed workflows, SQL AST validation
Machine learning: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, LoRA / QLoRA, contrastive training
Software: Python, TypeScript, SQL, FastAPI, React / Next.js, Docker, Nix, Linux
Scientific methods: transcriptome and DNA-methylation analysis, GO/KEGG enrichment, biological database development
recognition: Project lead, Provincial Undergraduate Innovation Training Program, Jilin University; completed 2022.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: I am seeking Ph.D. opportunities and research collaborations in AI agents, growing software platforms, and scientific AI.
contact.note: I am particularly interested in capability creation and reuse, verified scientific tool use, and evaluation across changing tasks and software versions.

entries.summary: Creator & Sole Developer · Independent open-source project · 2026 – Present
highlights: Building a local-first platform where agents turn human needs into persistent, reusable software modules.
Implemented iterative build sessions, content-addressed versions, tests, platform-owned execution probes, and migration checks on data copies.
Bound activation to reviewed versions, with conditional updates under existing user authorization.

entries.summary: Founder & Lead Developer · M.S. thesis project · 2025 – June 2026
highlights: Designed and implemented a configurable agent framework integrating eight CNCB biological data resources through MCP plugins.
Compiled visually configured workflows into checkpointed LangGraph state graphs, preserving structured entities and database/species scope across tool calls.
First-listed co-first author of the bioRxiv preprint. Architecture and open-source development through June 2026; technical support after graduation.

entries.summary: Technical Lead & Developer of the AI assistant · 2024 – 2025
highlights: Built the natural-language AI assistant for EWAS Open Platform, combining entity-enhanced schema linking, AST-level SQL validation, and execution-guided repair.
Designed a 30-question expert-reviewed evaluation with manually verified reference SQL over a fixed system version and database snapshot.
Co-first author of EWAS Open Platform 2026 in Nucleic Acids Research.

entries.summary: Independent protein–language model project · October 2024 – February 2025
highlights: Connected an ESM2 protein sequence encoder to Llama-3-8B using UniProt sequence–function data, with computing resources provided by my advisor.
Ran projector pretraining, 4-bit LoRA fine-tuning, and protein–text contrastive training; explored nonlinear projection in an exploratory prototype.

entries.organization: iDog & Scientific Data Applications · NGDC, CNCB
highlights: Performed canine transcriptome and DNA-methylation analysis for iDog and developed the DogRAG retrieval assistant.
Built the GSA submission-data retrieval application and Smart submission-consultation RAG plugin; contributed to BioKA biomarker curation.
Co-first author of iDog in Nucleic Acids Research; co-author of BioKA and contributor to NGDC consortium publications.

entries.summary: Undergraduate research · B.S. thesis, September 2022 – June 2023; innovation project completed 2022
highlights: Investigated MKP5 in hepatic fibrosis through mouse and cell models, histology, Western blot, qPCR, and GO/KEGG enrichment analysis.
Led a provincial undergraduate innovation project in chemical synthesis and crystallography.

research.title: Research
research.intro: I build agent systems that connect intent, software capabilities, and scientific evidence. My current focus is how platforms can grow through agent-authored modules, building on earlier work in configurable database agents and verified Text-to-SQL.
